speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Since then, dozens more workers have been injured or killed because they, too, were riding on the back of a lorry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have all seen these lorries full of workers cruising down our roads.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Back when she was just an eight-year-old, my daughter Ella pointed to such a lorry and said, "It's not safe, right?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If they crash, they will die." She took a photo of that lorry which I shared on social media.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Over 1,100 people liked that photo and many shared the same view about unsafe conditions, including Lisa Khoo who said, “Exactly...despite many accidents recently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We still see workers being transported this way on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Nothing seems to have changed despite a lot of talk about change.” We have known for many years that transporting people on the back of lorries is not safe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Over the years, we have done so much to make transport safer for our children taking the school bus, and soldiers in Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) tonners.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But, we still continue to transport our workers in unsafe conditions on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The worker sitting on the back of a lorry is also someone’s son, brother or father; someone’s loved one.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All I am asking today is that we give workers the same safety that we expect for anyone on our roads.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, we allow passengers to be transported on the back of lorries for “business purposes”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Business purposes are not good reasons for putting our workers at risk of death or injury every single day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We can all agree that safe transportation is good for everyone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have worked hard to ensure safe transportation for our school children, our soldiers and even our cargo.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have done well, very well in these aspects.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) appointed workshops to conduct the retrofitting.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To minimise business disruptions, workshops even provided replacement buses where feasible.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was a whole-of-nation effort that involved the Government, bus companies, bus drivers, bus attendants and the Singapore School Transport Association.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In July 2013, a school bus carrying nine kindergarten students crashed into a road barrier.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The children on board escaped without serious injuries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Media reports attributed this to the additional safety measures for school buses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And it is not just our people; even our cargo has to be transported in a safe way.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Road Traffic (Motor Vehicles, Construction and Use) Rules requires loads carried by vehicles to be secured in a way such that danger is unlikely to be caused by the load falling from the vehicle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The rules also require any load higher than the top of the side rails to be securely tied to the vehicle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would seem that in an accident, the goods will be more protected than the workers sitting on the back of lorries who might be flung out.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have introduced all these safety measures to keep our school children, soldiers and cargo safe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But why do we continue to allow our workers to be transported on the back of lorries when we already know this is unsafe?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure that we all agree that it is not safe to transport our workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In a media article, workers shared horror stories of friends being injured during sudden breaks or swerves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Workers talked about frequent injuries incurred en route to worksites.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A worker told the media that workers often talked about their mode of transport, but felt that it was pointless because their bosses were already well aware of the risks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many workers fear for their safety and lives, but feel that they do not have a choice or a voice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Over the past decade, there have been so many fatalities and injuries of people on board these lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many examples have been shared in this House so we all know this very well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we must remember that “downward trend” does not mean nobody is getting killed or injured.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: People continue to die or get injured because fundamentally, they are transported in unsafe conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For our school children, one death in 2008 was enough to catalyse an industry-wide change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We know that deaths or injuries will occur every year for our workers who are transported on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even the suppliers of the lorries have said that it is not safe to transport workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is also not a new issue I am raising.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Other Members of this House have spoken up repeatedly against using lorries to transport our workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many activists, many of whom are seated in our gallery today, have also spoken up on this, and I thank them for speaking up on this important issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is almost weird that we allow something which, whoever we ask, agrees it is unsafe to continue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What more do we need to stop transporting workers on the back of lorries?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) has raised “significant practical and operational considerations” for why it is not currently feasible to install seat belts or use other forms of transport for workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The first reason given is that transport by buses mean higher costs for small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: SMEs also require lorries which can transport both workers and goods to facilitate their business operations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand these valid concerns and will speak about these trade-offs later in my speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second reason MOT has given is that there are insufficient buses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Minister Iswaran said that a full transition to buses to ferry all workers will require many more buses than the available fleet of private buses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Insufficient buses, however, cannot be an excuse when we know for sure that people have died and have been injured every year and will continue to die and get injured.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How much more time do we need to increase our fleet of buses for a permanent solution to this problem?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We would never accept this excuse for our school children and soldiers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We cannot accept this excuse for our workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For all the parents seated here, would you be okay for your children to be transported on the back of lorries?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would you be okay for your son to be enlisted and transported in conditions which are unsafe?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The third reason MOT has given is that retrofitting lorries with seat belts is not safe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Minister Iswaran said that Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) shared that retrofitting of seats, seat belts and reinforcements compromises the structural integrity of the lorry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He said that OEMs said that this may create new safety risks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Of course, the views of the experts manufacturing and supplying the lorries are important.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But – and this is a big "but" – let us not forget that lorry suppliers have also said that it is not ideal to transport workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know that MOT has taken some steps to improve transport safety for workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We require lorries ferrying passengers to be fitted with rain covers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We also require lorry drivers to work no more than 12 hours a day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure Senior Minister of State Amy Khor will mention all these in her reply shortly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I commend these steps, but they simply do not go far enough to address the root of the problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The fundamental issue is that it is not safe to transport workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All the steps we have taken thus far do not address this fundamental issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three recommendations, including interim measures that we can take.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the Road Traffic Act, goods vehicles are already not allowed to be used for passengers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is unusual, unreasonable and unsafe that we have carved out a "business purpose" exception to the rule.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why do the safety issues disappear when the same exact vehicle is used for business purposes?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should remove this exception and implement a clear rule across the board that for safety reasons, no passengers should be transported on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If we cannot do this right now, then we should set a target year for this safety goal and plot a roadmap to achieve it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Setting a target year will also give the industry certainty and help build organic industry-driven solutions to achieve the goal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that we currently do not have enough buses to transport all workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A pilot with larger construction companies is a realistic interim step while we scale up to a full ban on transporting workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor shared that there have been consultations with trade associations in the construction sector and private bus operators.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To transport workers in key sectors by buses, we may need to double or triple the number of large buses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor also noted that there are private sector efforts to transport workers using buses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One example is Tong Tar Transport, which was asked by a multinational corporation (MNC) to ferry about 3,000 workers of their main and sub-contractors between dormitories to the construction sites via buses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor said that this was a large-scale endeavour that involved coordination among various bus operators but showed that it is possible under the right circumstances.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She encouraged more in the industry to follow.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is too important for the Government to just leave to the industry to figure out.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Senior Minister of State Amy pointed out, transport by buses is not impossible but requires coordination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may also involve staggered working hours for workers so that buses can pick them up over multiple trips.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We may not be able to fully transition to bus transport for all workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But a pilot like this is one step in the right direction, and the funding and coordination by the Government will help the workers and companies significantly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third recommendation is that we have designated drivers who only perform driving duties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, this is an interim measure until we achieve a full ban on transporting workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Imagine working 12 hours a day continuously for six hours in a physically exhausting role under the hot sun and resting for 30 minutes before having to drive a heavy vehicle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would we allow someone like that to drive a school bus?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Driving a heavy vehicle and transporting human lives is an important task.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should have specifically designated drivers who can fully focus on this task.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should start a pilot for this and, again, the Government can help provide some funding to kickstart this pilot.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That can go some way towards reducing the risk of accidents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I believe everyone in this House and in this country agrees that transporting workers on the back of lorries is not safe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All I am asking is that we treat our workers with the same care that we do for our children and soldiers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The worker on the back of the lorry is also someone's child, someone's loved one.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ms Teo shared in a Facebook comment on a video of workers being transported by lorries that, "Each worker is the son of a faraway family.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Like kids in Singapore, he is the apple of his mother's eye.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Accord dignity to the sons who have left their families.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is not a privilege only for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are better than this." Some have said that this is a migrant issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us not forget that it is not just migrant workers but Singaporean workers, sons, daughters, husbands and wives who are also riding dangerously on the back of lorries, too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should also remember what Prime Minister Lee said on workplace accidents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know that the reply from MOT to this speech will be about practical, operational and cost considerations as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But as my fellow colleague Mr Alex Yam put it when he spoke up about the transport of workers on the back of lorries, "We often quote trade-offs and costs as part of our decision-making matrix, but for the families in the recent accident who have lost their sons in Singapore, that cost would surmount all other costs we talked about".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We know that the reality is that none of us sitting here would like to be transported on the back of a lorry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should put our hearts and minds towards solving this fundamental issue of safety and the fundamental question of whether anyone should be transported in these kinds of unsafe conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I thank the Member for raising concerns about the transportation of workers in lorries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are equally concerned about the safety of our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our goal to improve safety in transportation is a work in progress and we will seek to do more and do better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But this is a goal that cannot be achieved solely through the efforts of the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For there to be enduring change, this goal needs to be shared by all stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Over the years, Government agencies have been reviewing and studying this issue on a regular basis to ensure that transportation of workers is done as safely as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Just last year, I announced four new measures during the Committee of Supply (COS) debate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, what is less salient perhaps, are the many hours of careful policy consideration, stakeholder engagement before and after the announcements that agencies put in to be able to roll them out with the stakeholders' support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The industry and workers themselves will need time to react, adapt and comply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Thereafter, the Government will also have to review the effectiveness of the measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are measures which affect both lives and livelihoods, including those of the workers themselves, and that is why we need to approach them carefully and holistically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is working with the industry to implement speed management devices in all lorries and will announce more details when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These are all in addition to the earlier requirements for lorries to be fitted with canopies and higher protective side railings, lower speed limits and minimum space requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We believe that these efforts will build on the earlier enhancements and further improve the safety of our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: And as I mentioned earlier, we will need to give the industry and workers time to adjust to the measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will then review them and continue to work with the industry to explore further enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Member has called on the Government to ban the transportation of workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have acknowledged this multiple times in the House.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, this is not a matter of legislating or imposing rules and expecting compliance from the industry, without regard for the wider implications and unintended consequences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Simply mandating that workers travel on buses or banning the transport of workers on lorries, without considering ground realities and constraints, is not a realistic solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Setting a timeline without understanding the varied concerns of all stakeholders is also not meaningful or workable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Transporting workers on lorries is a practice that cuts across various sectors and industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, we must understand the different challenges faced by each sector and ensure that our measures are effective, implementable and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, there are insufficient private buses to meet the needs across various sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A full transition to transportation via buses would require at least a doubling of the number of large private buses today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will have knock-on effects on the rest of society, including more congestion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, operating buses also requires a different driver's licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Members may have seen recent articles about the shortages of school bus drivers, resulting in some bus operators cancelling their service contracts despite underlying demand for school bus services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In fact, the shortage of bus drivers is not limited to the school bus sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A wider shift to mandate the use of buses will likely exacerbate this shortage and affect other bus service providers, including our public buses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, the nature of businesses of many micro, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), such as those in specialist trades, require them to be able to transport a small crew of people together with some equipment or goods to several locations in a single day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is neither practicable nor productive for them to have different vehicles to transport workers, equipment and goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Making it mandatory for them to do so may lead to decisions which impact the livelihoods of their workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On a similar note, while the intent of the Member's recommendation to have designated drivers is a good one, smaller enterprises, in particular, will find it challenging to employ full-time drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Member has suggested that the Government consider providing funding to larger construction companies, dormitories and bus operators to facilitate this shift.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our agencies are looking at specific sectors, engaging the companies that have been able or are open to shifting to buses or other modes of transportation, understanding the specific pain points and seeing how adoption can be scaled up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Today, there are already several bus companies that provide such services to transport workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are similarly studying these use cases to see how they can be scaled up as well as other possible modes of transportation that may be used.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Industry will be best placed to spearhead this effort as they best understand the ground needs and challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government will work with the industry and consider any further support required, but this will need to be effective and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our agencies are working hard on the ground and I seek the support of the House as we continue to work together with our workers, associations and industry to bring about further effective and sustainable improvements to the safety of our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In the meantime, we are pressing ahead with the implementation and monitoring of the set of measures we had last announced at COS 2022 to enhance worker safety, even as we look at how we can further transit from the use of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I just ask whether MOT can consider that roadmap, similar to what we have done with climate change?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We have a net-zero emissions target for 2050, something that we said was not possible a few years back.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Now, it is possible, and we have set up a roadmap for that.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, I am wondering how often does MOT ignore the advice of suppliers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If we look back, fundamentally, the people who supply the lorries tell us, "Do not put people on the back." How often is it that the Government does not listen to the advice of the people who supply us with equipment?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think I have given a detailed response to the Member's suggestions and views.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What he is asking is still similar with regard to our plans to transit to safer modes of transportation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, I think this is something that we have to work out with the industry, with the associations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, we have already implemented various measures and we are implementing a new set of measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to your point about ignoring the advice of suppliers, no.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The advice of the supplier is that it is not useful, meaningful or safe to do, because lorries were not built for safety belts.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.30 pm.
